# Full application test plan (Gate 2)

Date: 2026-11-10. Status: **test inventory only. Every case below is `Not Run`.** Nothing has been executed in this gate, and no application code was changed.

Companion files: `full-application-test-plan.csv` (same rows, for filtering), `tools/build_test_plan.py` and `tools/render_test_plan.py` (regenerate both files from the SRS and fail if any SRS line has no test case).

## 1. How to read this plan

- **Source of truth:** the SRS `.docx`. Every requirement line in it (bullets, statements and arrow chains, 1,223 lines) was extracted by script and given at least one test case. The Requirement column quotes the SRS wording exactly and says where it is.
- **Extra cases** (163) were added for things the SRS requires in general but does not list line by line: the System Administrator workstream you approved, your security, performance and workflow lists, role and route matrices, and one cross-institution and one unauthorised-access case per module.
- **Implementation status** separates what exists from what does not, as found in the Gate 1 audit: `Existing` (present in code, never executed in this cycle), `Partial`, `Missing`, `On hold` (your decision), `Future scope` (your decision or the SRS marks it future), `Unverified` (not inspected in depth or never measured), `Process` (an organisational responsibility, checked by document review). **Existing does not mean tested or passing.**
- **Steps are generated per kind of requirement** (create, view, edit, assign, approve, export, calculate, AI, security, database, document, workflow). They are exact enough to run but use placeholders for data; each is made fully data-specific when it is automated in Gate 3. Curated cases (System Administrator, security, performance, workflows, matrices) are hand-written.
- **Gate 3 expectation** says what I expect to happen when the case is run, so a failure on a Missing feature is not a surprise. A case for a Missing feature is expected to fail until the feature is built in Gate 4.
- **Test types** are Unit, Integration, API, E2E, Security, Performance, Accessibility, Database inspection, Document review. **Status** is one of Pass, Fail, Blocked, Not Run; all are Not Run.
- **IDs:** `M01`-`M21` modules; `SA` System Administrator; `ROLE-*` roles; `SRS-STRUCT`, `-UI`, `-DATA`, `-AI`, `-NFR`, `-SECURITY`, `-INT`, `-REPORT`, `-FLOW`, `-REL`, `-ACCEPT`, `-DELIV`, `-PROC`, `-PRINC`, `-VISION`, `-OBJ`, `-DEF` for the other SRS sections.

## 1b. Changes to the plan after approval (with rationale)

The 1,386 case IDs are unchanged. Wording was changed only where stated here.

| Date | Case | Change | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-11 | SA-TC-054 | Step 3 and the expected result now say what the database-outage check must show: `/api/health/ready` 503, the monitoring API 503 `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE`, no credential receives data, a connection failure or a marked stale last-known state, recovery without restart. | The original expectation (the authenticated dashboard reports "database unavailable") needs the platform administrator to be authenticated, which needs the database and a freshly checked second step. Showing data without them would bypass MFA enforcement. Decision B (no authentication fallback) therefore moves the outage signal to the unauthenticated readiness endpoint, with an external uptime monitor recommended. |
| 2026-11-11 | SA-TC-055 | Added step 3 (retry, concurrency, monitoring failure) and extended the expected result (per-slot records, no duplicates, no effect on the job, nothing sensitive stored, 90 days). Implementation note changed from "not recorded today" to built. | The approved `JobRun` design (decision A and C) defines what "accurate job status" means; the added step covers the approved requirements (retries, concurrent executions, partial failure). |
| 2026-11-11 | SA-TC-008 | Audit note only: agreed scope. Steps and expected result are unchanged. | The SRS names no request-latency or throughput metric. Approved scope: use Vercel Observability for application-wide request performance (the deployment may run several independent function instances, so in-memory metrics would be instance-local and unreliable); the custom dashboard covers health, dependencies, jobs and errors only. The case stays Blocked pending formal clarification or integration of performance monitoring; it is not passed. |
| 2026-11-11 | SA-TC-060 | Steps 1 and 2 and the expected result now say how limits and "fallback" are tested: institution, provider and zero limits are exceeded; a failing provider is reported with **no automatic failover**; the environment settings apply when nothing is stored. The Audit note column of SA-TC-006 and 058 to 062 records that they were built in Gate 4.4. | The original step 2 ("fail the primary provider and check fallback") assumed an automatic switch to another provider. The approved design forbids that: a call must never silently move to a different key, provider or model than the one an administrator chose, because that changes cost, data handling and results without anyone deciding it (the instruction that there is no automatic failover). The fallback the platform does have, to the server environment when no configuration is stored, is what the check now covers. |

## 4. System Administrator coverage

Scope follows your Gate 2 decisions: institution search, editing, activation and suspension, platform-wide analytics, platform audit-log viewer, real monitoring, protected AI provider and model configuration with masked secrets, platform-level support. Subscriptions and billing are documented as future scope. Platform administrator creation stays script-based; the cases below verify its security and MFA.

**Cases:** 67 (12 from SRS 3.1 lines, 55 curated). Existing-feature cases 26, partial 6, missing or proposed 32, future scope 2.

## 5. Additional roles (decision 3): exactly what the SRS requires

## 6. Reports (decision 4): the ten missing downloads and the rest

The SRS says only "downloadable reports in PDF, Excel and CSV where appropriate"; it does not say which format each report needs (see ambiguity A-10). ## 8. Unresolved SRS ambiguities and audit assumptions

### Your two questions, answered with citations

**Module 19 (decision 5): no live multi-student collaboration room is required.** The SRS lists exactly, under "MODULE 19: GROUP DISCUSSION AND COMMUNICATION SIMULATOR": "AI-generated topics.", "Multiple AI participants.", "Voice-based discussions.", "Timed sessions.", "Debate simulation.", "Counterarguments.", "Presentation practice.", "Communication evaluation.", "Listening and response evaluation.", "Improvement recommendations." A search of the whole SRS text for "collaborat", "live room", "multi-student", "peer", "real-time" and "real time" finds no match. The words "Multiple AI participants" and the title "Simulator" describe AI-played participants. Conclusion: the current AI-participant design stays. Test cases M19-TC-001 to M19-TC-010 cover each listed item.

**Approval gates for different drive types (decision 6): not in the SRS.** A search for "drive type", "type of drive", "off-campus", "pool" and "gate" finds nothing about approval by kind of drive. "Approval" appears only in these places: resource "Approval status." and the resource workflow "Review → Approve" (Module 7), internship "College approval." and "Company approval." (Module 9), resume "Student approval." (Module 10), "JD review and approval." and "No JD should be published without authorised review." (Module 11), "After JD approval and candidate matching" (Module 13), and "Resume approval." (section 7). **Audit assumption, not an SRS requirement:** a gate that depends on drive type. No test case is created for it.
